svg.title: VAR vs dynamic factor model
svg.desc: VAR parameters grow with the square of the variable count, while a dynamic factor model reduces the dimension to a few common factors and handles missing data and mixed frequencies in state-space form.
svg.text: Regress every series on every other, or reduce to a few common factors?
Causality and impulse responses across variables
Parameters grow with the square of the series count
Parameters grow linearly with the number of series
Stays manageable as series are added
Links grow as n², making both estimation and reading hard
All series share a few factors
The loadings Λ are the observation matrix; the rest is idiosyncratic noise
A VAR's parameters grow with the square of the number of variables and soon hit the estimation limit.
A DFM cuts the dimension to a few common factors and absorbs missing data through the state-space form.
Factors are the state, loadings the observation matrix —
the Kalman filter absorbs gaps and mixed frequencies
Next: what changes when a reduced-form VAR is written in state-space form.
